GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The large-document problem decomposes into sequential GRACE changes because its two O(document) cost trajectories (full-document mount on open; full synchronous derived work plus history deep-copy per edit) need different fixes, and every later fix risks silent data regression unless current behavior is frozen first. Stage 0 is deliberately limited to measurements and behavioral oracles: it produces the evidence that forces the owner's product decisions (target size, absolute and relative budgets, Wave A/B order, crash-durability contract and later-wave experimental access model) and the frozen oracle that all later waves diff against. One mega-spec for every wave was rejected because each wave needs its own approval and its own evidence gate; starting Wave A (progressive mount) without a baseline was rejected because success budgets would be guesses; treating upstream marktext PR #4946 or ColaMD's lazyMarkdownPipeline as ready patches was rejected — they are design references only.

Alternatives.Alternative: Single mega-spec covering Waves A–D: rejected — unapprovable scope, no evidence gates between waves, and the owner's Wave A/B order decision would be presupposed.
Start with Wave A (progressive mount) and measure later: rejected — no baseline means no honest budget, and behavioral oracles would be written after the behavior changed.
Adopt upstream marktext PR #4946 or ColaMD lazyMarkdownPipeline as patches: rejected — OPEN/unmerged external work with different architecture assumptions; kept as design references only.
Rely on Source Code mode as the large-file fallback: rejected — CodeMirror viewportMargin: Infinity likely renders the whole document; it stays unmeasured until Stage 0 numbers exist.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Fixture generator governance: test modules vs scripts, exact location, MODULE_CONTRACT role (TEST/SCRIPT) and MODULE_MAP mode (LOCALS) — fixed by the plan.

Which metrics become CI gates vs recorded diagnostics; sample count, warmup policy, percentile calculation and outlier policy; relative vs absolute budget policy and platform labels — proposed with numbers by the plan, approved by the owner after Stage 0 evidence.

Later-wave experimental access model — visible Experimental setting, support-only preference, or private test artifact; whichever model is selected remains local, default-off and session-latched until a separate approved default flip.
Artifact naming, location and retention for baseline JSON and acceptance captures (private captures stay uncommitted).

Whether Stage 0 itself updates the owning routed .grace/context document after owner decisions, or a separate governance bundle records target size, absolute/relative budgets, wave order, crash contract and experimental access model before any Wave A/B spec — flagged fork, default: separate governance bundle.

The file-level boundary inside the required M-060 harness module, which owns Stage 0 benchmark drivers, deterministic fixture tooling and characterization-session harness, and the exact M-011/M-012 summaries or dependency links that record its renderer/Muya dependencies — fixed by the plan against actual write scope.
Admission of any new stable CI gate into .github/workflows/test.yml — intentionally exceptional, never automatic.
10 MB target size (and therefore any 10 MB fixture promotion from optional diagnostic to required) — owner decision at the Stage 0 gate.

Scenarios.Scenario: Program shape after Stage 0 (design context for later changes, each with its own spec/plan/approval): Wave A progressive mount (opening-first contract); Wave B1 change-source contract; Wave B2 lazy derived-state pipeline with one freshness primitive; Wave B3 incremental history materialization; Wave C size guards and graceful degradation; Wave D (conditional) virtualization or engine migration only if A+B+C miss the approved contract. Rollout: each behavior-changing strategy behind its own default-off session-latched flag; legacy path retained until removal gates; a later explicit release instruction is always separate.

The packet's safety and verification matrix (06) rows R-01..R-40 (fresh-Markdown readers and save/durability boundaries), D-01..D-31 (data-integrity oracle), M-01..M-20 (progressive-mount oracle), F-01..F-09 (feature flags/rollout), S-01..S-09 (security/privacy) and X-01..X-05 (execution/merge safety) are the standing inventory future wave specs must carry into their corner matrices without losing rows or explicitly justifying non-applicability. Stage 0 implements only the characterization/foundation subset; the rest is context, not scope.

Sequencing with active changes: Stage 0's likely writes (src/renderer/bench, fixtures, tests, graph/verification performance routing) overlap the broad .grace/graph/*.xml and .grace/verification/*.xml scopes already claimed by C-50, C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY, C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM and others per the live parallel preflight. The plan must not be approved or executed until every overlap is sequenced, narrowed or completed; C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY (position flush) and C-DOC-CHANGE-JOURNAL (change journal) states are re-read immediately before planning because the derived-state waves depend on their interfaces.
